metadata.title: Results from the Teacher Knowledge Survey: What Teachers Know About General Pedagogy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This publication reports results from the OECD Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS) implemented as a module within TALIS 2024, administered to lower secondary (ISCED level 2) teachers and, where relevant, principals in the same sampled schools. The reader’s guide states that principal-reported school characteristics are analysed at the teacher level and weighted by teacher weights when principal data are linked to teachers (e.g., school size). However, the excerpt provided does not name the specific weight variable(s) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the exact weighting implementation cannot be verified from the text shown. Analysts should therefore use the official TALIS/TKS sampling weights provided with the underlying microdata for teacher-level estimates and apply the corresponding teacher weights when incorporating principal-linked school attributes; replicate-weight handling should follow the TALIS 2024 technical documentation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report excerpt does not describe any plausible-values (PV) generation or PV-based achievement scaling; instead, it presents a teacher general pedagogical knowledge (GPK) assessment and many outcomes based on self-reports from teachers and principals. Because the provided text does not document a missing-data handling strategy for any PV-based or imputed outcomes, the missing-data approach cannot be extracted from the excerpt. This is therefore a reporting gap for missing-data handling details in the material provided.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: TKS 2024 was administered to lower secondary (ISCED level 2) teachers as a module within the Core TALIS 2024 school sample. The excerpt does not provide the exact analytic-sample inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., participation-rate thresholds, item non-response cutoffs, or any specific adjudication rules applied to the GPK assessment and questionnaires). It does note that caution is advised for countries/territories that did not meet TALIS technical standards for participation rates and that Annex C contains information on TKS target population, samples, and adjudication outcomes; therefore, the analytic sample is restricted to the TALIS 2024 sampled schools and their ISCED 2 teachers, with further restrictions likely applied according to TALIS technical standards and adjudication rules.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS module report presents results from the Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS) 2024, which measures teachers’ general pedagogical knowledge (GPK) through an assessment administered to lower secondary (ISCED level 2) teachers within the Core TALIS 2024 sampled schools. The report also analyses many teacher and principal questionnaire variables based on self-reports, and it explicitly cautions that self-reported measures may be affected by cultural response patterns, social desirability bias, and validity concerns related to recall and interpretation. The report provides international averages as arithmetic means across participating countries (TKS average-8) and a subset OECD average-4 (Chile, Poland, Portugal, United States). It further states that the design of TKS does not allow causal claims between variables; results should be interpreted as statistical associations. The excerpt does not provide the underlying statistical model specifications, PV/missing-data procedures, or exact sample sizes, which are likely detailed in the TALIS 2024 technical documentation and annexes.
